transcript:
Header:
Date: 2025-12-10
Time: 14:00 UTC
Duration: 54 minutes
Attendees: Samira Patel (Redwood AE), Ethan Voss (Redwood SE), Jared Cole (SynthAnalytics CTO), Maya Lin (ML Eng), Priya Singh (Infra), Diego Alvarez (Prod)

Summary (auto): quick recap of last week, then main focus on benchmark comparisons vs BaselineCloud, discussion of tail latency and throughput tradeoffs, agreed to run additional KV-cache tests and exchange traces.

00:00 Speaker 1 (Samira): Hey everyone thanks for joining on time, I think we have about 50 minutes today, quick agenda: go over the benchmark spreadsheet updates, call out the p95/p99 numbers, then Ethan will talk through tuning results, and we will close with next steps.
00:28 Speaker 2 (Jared): Sounds good, yeah we ran your 1.2k request sample last night and peeking at the numbers now.
00:40 Speaker 3 (Ethan): Cool i'll start with the headline — compared to BaselineCloud's hosted endpoint, Redwood's dedicated config gave about 20% lower p95 and roughly 30% lower p99 tail latency on our medium-length chat workload when using continuous batching plus prefix KV-cache. p50 was pretty similar across both.
01:05 Speaker 4 (Maya): Wait can you give absolute numbers? the spreadsheet shows p95 240ms vs 300ms?
01:12 Speaker 2 (Ethan): Yeah so for the rtx-style GPU runs: Redwood dedicated (quantized int8) p50 ~45ms p95 ~240ms p99 ~410ms throughput 180 tokens/s. BaselineCloud hosted (fp16) p50 ~48ms p95 ~300ms p99 ~600ms throughput 230 tokens/s when they crank batch size to 128.
01:40 Speaker 3 (Priya): Ok so baseline can push more tokens/s but much worse tail. For us tail matters because our UI is sensitive to 95th.
01:55 Speaker 1 (Samira): Exactly, and our suggestion was to tune batching thresholds to hit a balance — smaller batches for low-latency routes, larger batches for bulk embedding/rerank jobs.
02:10 Speaker 5 (Diego): There's also cost to consider, baseline's high throughput at large batches was cheaper per token in their quote. Did you run cost-per-1k tokens?
02:21 Speaker 3 (Ethan): Yes we did in the sheet — with our autoscaling profile and prefix caching, effective cost per 1k tokens is within 10% of BaselineCloud for this workload because caching reduced repeated prefix compute. Without caching, Baseline looks cheaper on raw throughput econ.
02:42 Speaker 2 (Jared): The spreadsheet looks clean but a couple of numbers are an odd outlier — there's a run with 1s p99 for Redwood? is that from cold start?
02:53 Speaker 3 (Ethan): Good catch — that was a cold-start mix where the KV cache miss rate spiked. We labeled that run 'cold-mix-2' — I can remove it or annotate better. The steady-state runs are the ones to compare.
03:12 Speaker 1 (Samira): On the topic of cache — we ran a KV-cache heavy experiment this week where prefixes repeated across sessions. In that scenario our effective p95 went down to 180ms and cost-per-1k dropped by ~22%.
03:33 Speaker 4 (Maya): That is promising — our workload is prefix-heavy for a lot of flows. How confident are you in the cache hit modeling vs our prod traces?
03:46 Speaker 3 (Ethan): Confidence is medium — the synthetic trace was constructed from logs you shared two weeks ago but we need more representative production trace to get precise numbers.
04:00 Speaker 2 (Priya): we'll share 3 days of anonymized traces, security permitting.
04:07 Speaker 1 (Samira): Great — we'll use that to run realistic batching simulation.
04:15 Speaker 6 (Speaker 6): quick question on quantization — what's the accuracy delta with int8 versus your baseline fp16 run?
04:26 Speaker 3 (Ethan): In our evals on the dev set we saw <1% quality regression with int8 on the LLM variant you're using; for reranking tasks it's negligible, for some long-form generative tasks there is a slight drift — we can show the eval sheets.
04:45 Speaker 4 (Maya): Can we see the evals?
04:48 Speaker 3 (Ethan): yes i'll attach the eval CSVs.
04:55 Speaker 2 (Jared): On infra options — what's the expected difference if we go Redwood hosted vs dedicated vs private VPC? tail numbers?
05:06 Speaker 1 (Samira): Hosted gives fastest onboarding and simplest network path but shared noisy neighbors can affect extremes; Dedicated gives predictable throughput and better p99 in our runs; Private VPC is similar to dedicated but adds customer control and potential network egress variability depending on your cloud setup. We'll run a VPC-focused trial if you want.
05:27 Speaker 2 (Priya): For compliance we prefer VPC/private but initially would like to validate perf on hosted or dedicated first.
05:36 Speaker 3 (Ethan): Another thing — autoscaling policy shapes tail latencies. We tried conservative scale-up thresholds and got worse p99; aggressive policy reduces p99 but increases cost. The spreadsheet includes a few autoscale parameter sets.
05:58 Speaker 4 (Maya): Can you run a scenario with an aggressive scale policy but a hard cap to show cost impact?
06:04 Speaker 3 (Ethan): yes we can run that and include cost per hour at peak.
06:10 Speaker 1 (Samira): Okay next i want to call out a curiosity — BaselineCloud's runs were optimized by cranking batch size to 128 which pushes throughput but obviously hurts p99. We think for your interactive endpoints smaller batches + caching is better.
06:28 Speaker 2 (Jared): Makes sense, our web product prioritizes p95 impact on conversions, so we care more about tail.
06:36 Speaker 5 (Diego): Are there any known regressions when moving to int8 on longer sequences? we saw some tokenization oddities last month with another vendor.
06:48 Speaker 3 (Ethan): We didn't see tokenization regressions; long-seq generation had minor fluency differences but we can run the prompt suite you shared.
07:05 Speaker 4 (Maya): let's do that — attach the prompt suite and evals.
07:09 Speaker 1 (Samira): We'll include both the prompt suite and the per-model evals and flag any failures.
07:16 Speaker 3 (Ethan): For the KV-cache test plan — we propose two runs: (1) prefix heavy with 80% cache hit simulated; (2) cold start mix with low hit rate. We'll run both on dedicated and hosted and share p50/p95/p99 and throughput.
07:32 Speaker 2 (Priya): Good. Also want to see memory metrics and GPU utilization during the runs.
07:40 Speaker 3 (Ethan): We'll include GPU util, CPU, network, queue depth histograms.
07:45 Speaker 1 (Samira): Any blockers from your side in getting traces and auth for us to spin up a VPC test?
07:52 Speaker 2 (Priya): Need to confirm with security, that's why we'll share anonymized traces first then sync.
08:00 Speaker 3 (Ethan): We'll also share a short how-to on redwood's VPC networking requirements and kube-ish config for the private deployment so you can review with infra.
08:12 Speaker 1 (Samira): Quick callout on the security doc — we have SOC2 stuff, KMS/HSM options, and SAML SSO details. We'll push that in the follow-up email.
08:23 Speaker 4 (Maya): Perfect.
08:30 Speaker 3 (Ethan): Returning to benchmarks — there's also an interesting pattern on queuing latency when throughput spikes; BaselineCloud queues at the load-balancer which increased observed p99. Redwood's edge routing reduces that by moving batching logic closer to the model.
08:52 Speaker 2 (Jared): That routing detail is important; can you diagram that in the doc?
08:58 Speaker 3 (Ethan): Yep i'll add a simple diagram showing request flow, batching boundary, and cache layer.
09:06 Speaker 1 (Samira): Let's go rapid-fire for any open questions.
09:10 Speaker 4 (Maya): Pricing — any adjustments for reserved capacity? if we commit a monthly reserve can we get better unit costs to beat Baseline even on raw throughput?
09:19 Speaker 1 (Samira): Yes reserved Dedicated commitments reduce unit cost significantly and make sense when you have predictable load. We'll include a pricing sketch for 3/6/12 month commit levels.
09:32 Speaker 5 (Diego): SLOs for p99 — what's realistic if we go dedicated?
09:36 Speaker 3 (Ethan): In our runs with dedicated and aggressive autoscale we consistently got p99 under 450ms for your workload; we'll aim to put sample SLOs in the follow-up.
09:49 Speaker 2 (Priya): anything else on tooling? traces/observability?
09:53 Speaker 3 (Ethan): We can give you access to a temporary Console view for the pilot so you can see token-level cost and latency breakdowns, per-route dashboards and trace links.
10:05 Speaker 1 (Samira): Ok, recap of next steps: Samira sends spreadsheets and pricing sketch; Ethan runs KV-cache focussed tests and shares logs; Priya shares traces; schedule infra deep-dive for the VPC/perf run.
10:23 Speaker 2 (Jared): good, we'll target to get traces by next Wednesday.
10:30 Speaker 1 (Samira): Awesome thanks everyone, we'll follow up in email and ping for calendar times.
10:36 Speaker 6 (Speaker 6): thanks, bye.

End Recap:
- Redwood shows lower p95/p99 tail latency in steady-state with caching + batching; BaselineCloud can push higher throughput at large batch sizes but with worse tail latency and potential queuing.
- Action items assigned and dates agreed.
- Follow-ups: KV-cache runs, production traces, pricing/commit sketches, VPC deep-dive.
